title: Why Forgive and Forget is Bad Advice - Nautilus
gist: Nautilus introduces an interview with Duke memory researcher and new MacArthur fellow Felipe de Brigard on how forgiveness reshapes memory of atrocity, framing the paradox that forgetting past hurts risks repeat harm while unresolved memories can fuel repeated violence and perpetual war.

insights.claim: Forgiveness presents a paradox: forgetting past hurts can leave people vulnerable to repeat offenses from the same or similar perpetrators, while letting go can relieve resentment, anger and hate.

insights.so_what: Frames how societies weigh reconciliation versus vigilance after conflicts.

insights.claim: The article's headline contends that the common advice to 'forgive and forget' is bad advice, since forgiveness reshapes rather than erases the memory of atrocity.
insights.speaker: Kristen French
insights.so_what: Challenges conventional reconciliation narratives in post-conflict settings.

insights.claim: Duke University researcher Felipe de Brigard has studied memory and forgiveness since the early 2000s with John Templeton Foundation support and has just won a MacArthur Foundation grant to continue the work.
